newsitem.title: JAPAN: History of Japan's worst oil spills.
newsitem.headline: History of Japan's worst oil spills.

text.p: Following is a chronology of Japan's worst oil spills.
1. Nov 1971 - The tanker Juliana on its way to Showa Shell Sekiyu KK's refinery in Niigata, northern Japan, was grounded in Niigata Bay, causing about 6,000 tonnes of crude oil to spill into the bay.

2. Dec 1974 - An oil tank at Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd's Mizushima refinery in western Japan ruptured, causing fuel oil to overflow into the sea. An estimated 7,200 to 9,100 tonnes of fuel oil leaked into the sea as a result of the accident.

3. Jan 1997 - Coastal fishing villages in northwestern Japan braced for economic and environmental catastrophe as oil slicks from the sunken Russian tanker Nakhodka coated beaches and threatened prized shellfish beds. The spill from the ruptured tanker, carrying some 19,000 tonnes of heavy fuel oil was about 5,200 tonnes.
4 July 1997 - A supertanker struck a shallow reef in Tokyo Bay leaking an estimated 13,400 tonnes of crude oil, producing what is believed to be Japan's worst ever oil spill.
